terms.gloss: a flood, the overflowing of a river
terms.comment: The water spreading over the land; the verb is inundō, classical in Cicero and Livy, of a river or rain flooding the fields, and also, without an object, of the river overflowing (Arnus inundāverat, Liv. 22.2.2).

terms.gloss: a flood, a deluge; the Flood
terms.register: vōx poētica et post-Augustēa: Verg., Ov.; Sen., Plin. Ep.
evidence: Sen. Q.N. 3.27 (the great flood, Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also dīluviēs (Lucr., Hor.). In Seneca and in Christian Latin the Flood (dīluvium, Vulg. Matt. 24.38).
Cicero’s word, beside exustiō, for the floods and burnings of the earth.

phrases.latin: num istīc quoque immīte et turbidum caelum? hīc assiduae tempestātēs et crēbra dīluvia
phrases.english: is the sky wild and stormy there too? here it is storm after storm and flood after flood
